workstream: Round-2 judge, website lens: engineering cost and risk of designs A-D (research only)
status: Judgement only; this file is the only one written. No repo file, workflow, site file or commit changed.
ruling_architecture: validation-evidence/main-architecture.json: static pages built by website/build.py, rebuilt from empty by .github/workflows/website.yml, published by GitHub Pages. Checkout HEAD e7f8cbc (main-architecture cites 349df2a); cited lines were checked on the checkout.
lens: Engineering cost and risk on the website: fit with the 10-minute cron and 15-minute job; build-from-empty and --previous handling for any loop; vendored and wire bytes on slow links; WebGL2 on phones; test, smoke, path-filter and command changes; failures that must surface as problem or stale; maintenance (JS lines, moving parts); what the prototypes proved.
scale: 0 = cannot be built within the written rules; 10 = lowest risk on the website, rule-compliant, with measured budgets. Scores cover this lens only; the owner's globe request and the 3D gap are not scored. Desktop parts of A and B are scored only for what transfers.
method: Read the architecture file, designs A-D, both round-1 judges, globe-libs, prototype-globe, hosting-options, rights-matrix, README sections 1-7, the supervisor log, AGENTS.md, DESIGN.md, DECISIONS D27-D29 and the repo lines named. Live: the three@0.186.1 npm tarball (sizes, GNU gzip -9, LICENSE, file headers); the live Pages site (headers, wire sizes, data/state.json); gh run list for the Website workflow; WebFetch of the Actions terms, Pages limits, Natural Earth terms, a NASA page and caniuse. Computed figures use measured ratios and the designs' own budgets.
summary: Ranking: design C (C2 first: Leaflet overlays, no library) 8; design D (globe page with vendored three.js) 6; design A 3; design B 2. Design D is the only option that delivers a globe inside the website rules, and it is buildable, but it carries the largest cost: an unprototyped library, 850 new JS lines, a loop with no persistence path, and a 417 KB gzip library. The most important finding sits outside every design. The scheduled build does not run every 10 minutes on this repo: three scheduled starts (2026-10-16 19:42Z, 22:14Z; 2026-10-17 00:35Z; median gap 146.5 min) and none in the 4 h 10 min before the check; the live state.json was 250 minutes old. Every freshness claim assumes the 10-minute cadence. Design D's first visit is about 1.1 MB on the wire, not 2.8 MB, and its phase-4 loop is about 10 MB per visit, which D does not count.

key_findings.finding: Cadence (measured): scheduled starts of the Website workflow on main were 2026-10-16T19:42:35Z, 22:14:06Z and 2026-10-17T00:35:40Z (3 of 42 runs). Median gap 146.5 min (range 141.6-151.5). None from 00:35:40Z to the check at 04:46:49Z. Live data/state.json built 00:36:01Z, 250 min old. About 73 ten-minute slots since 16:35Z (computed): about 4% started. Cause not diagnosed.
key_findings.evidence: gh run list (2026-10-17); live data/state.json; website.yml:15.

key_findings.finding: Runner time (measured): main runs median 70 s (69-76 s, n=3); all 41 successful runs median 87 s (24-140 s). The 15-minute limit (website.yml:38) has about 10x headroom. The 32-51 s figures in main-architecture.json are sandbox runs.

Pages serves text gzip-compressed (HTML, JS, JSON, CSS; server GitHub.com; HTTP/2). Raw to wire: map.js 114,696 to 36,296 B; leaflet.js 147,552 to 43,194; basemap.json 384,594 to 109,831; data/map.json 47,480 to 5,922; map.css 46,944 to 11,724; style.css 19,944 to 4,902; map.html 10,416 to 3,331. Pages output is 1.8% above GNU gzip -9 (map.js 36,296 vs 35,662). Images and woff2 do not compress; raw budgets overstate text about 3x.
key_findings.evidence: Live site, 2026-10-17; repo map.js matches live decoded bytes (sha256 prefix a04d3f4c).

key_findings.finding: Cache (headers measured; reuse inferred): static files send cache-control max-age=600. ETag is hex(mtime)-hex(size): map.js 6ad2c31a-1c008 is 2026-10-17T00:36:42Z (equal to Last-Modified) and 114,696 B. That is 41 s after state.json's build time, so the ETag may change at each deploy even when bytes do not (one sample). If so, returning visitors re-download unchanged vendored files after each deploy. build.py:361-364 assumes reuse. Test in phase 1 with two deploys of identical bytes.
key_findings.evidence: curl headers on the live site; build.py:361-365.

key_findings.finding: three@0.186.1 (MIT; published 2026-09-24, 23 days old; passes design B's 14-day rule): build/three.module.js 662,772 B and build/three.core.js 1,458,113 B, exactly as designs D and globe-libs state. GNU gzip -9: 130,745 + 286,358 = 417,103 B (about 424,500 B on Pages, computed). No minified build ships (build/ holds .js, .cjs, .tsl and webgpu files only), so the raw 2.12 MB stays on disk and in each build's copy. Design D's 'about 0.62 MB' gzip figure is 1.46x high. Both files carry an SPDX MIT header.
key_findings.evidence: npm tarball and metadata (2026-10-17); globe-libs.json comparison row.

key_findings.finding: Page weight (computed): design D's first visit is about 1.11 MB on the wire (three.js 0.42 MB; Earth 0.40 MB and basemap 0.15 MB are budgets; fonts at 75 KB). D states 2.78 MB raw and 14 s at 1.6 Mbit/s; wire bytes give 5.5 s (17.7 s at 0.5 Mbit/s). Today's Map page is about 0.29 MB before frames. Design C's first visit with its 0.66 MB budget is about 0.95 MB. First visit does not separate C2 from D; the loop does (K7).
key_findings.evidence: K3; design-d.json s3 per_visitor_first_load and s2 slow_link_arithmetic; design-c.json size_impact.

key_findings.finding: Loop bytes per viewer (computed): design D phase 4 loads 12 native MRMS frames at 0.84 MB, about 10 MB per visit (11.1 MB with the page). C2 P4 loads 12 class-raster frames at 0.9 MB for 2 h (about 1.2 MB per visit). At the 100 GB soft limit: about 9,000 D loop visits a month against about 84,000 for C2. D counts build-side reads, not viewer bytes.
key_findings.evidence: design-d.json s3 mrms and pages_bandwidth; design-c.json P4; hosting-options.json pages limits.

key_findings.finding: Build-side reads (computed): design D phase 4 reads 11 earlier frames from the live site each build: 39.7 GB a month at 10-minute cadence, 2.7 GB at the observed median gap. C2 reads 12 frames of about 75 KB: 3.9 GB a month at 10 minutes. load_previous fetches only data/state.json (build.py:472-478) and returns None on any error with no status, so a failed frame read would look like an empty loop.

MRMS budget not measured for the designed product: 835,879 B is the peak keyframe for 33 levels at 20 dBZ (pipeline-options.json, keyframe plus delta encoding). Design D's frame is 11 levels at 20, 35 and 50 dBZ, so its 1.0 MB phase-3 budget is untested for its own configuration.
key_findings.evidence: pipeline-options.json peak_keyframe and derivation; design-d.json s3 mrms.

key_findings.finding: Test scope: the remote-URL regex runs on map.html only (tests/test_site.py:464); the googleapis check covers index, about and map (470-471). JavaScript fetch URLs and CSS url() are not seen. The browser request check runs only on branch pushes (website.yml:96-105); merges to main publish (AGENTS.md:56). Playwright is unpinned (website.yml:99).

Deploy coupling: the deploy job needs build (website.yml:162) and runs only when publish is true (163). A raising product step fails build; under GitHub's default job-status rule (not re-fetched) deploy is skipped and the last deployment ages. build_gridded never raises (gridded.py:991-1008); new product steps need the same contract.

Vocabulary: map.js:34 says 'No radar coverage' for hatched areas; sources.py:116-117 says 'Negative values mean no radar coverage'. Design D's rule for -99 and -999 is 'No radar data' (meanings unverified, mrms.json). One state, two words: decide once.

JS footprint: design D adds 850 lines and 55,000 B (globe.js 600 lines and 40,000 B; volume.js 250 and 15,000): +39% lines and +48% bytes over map.js (2,155 lines, 114,696 B; computed). Design C adds six duties (N1-N6); N5, a per-minute JS clock, is new time arithmetic that rule 4 does not list.
key_findings.evidence: wc on map.js; design-d.json s2 loader_budget; design-c.json js_duties; judge-rules.json.

key_findings.finding: WebGL2 (caniuse, live): iOS Safari 15-26.6 and 27.0-27.2 supported; 12-14.8 disabled by default. Chrome for Android: only 154 shown. Samsung Internet 7.2-30 supported. Global usage 97.13%. iOS 14 and older lack WebGL2 by default, so a text fallback is required. No device run exists.

Licences (live): Natural Earth: 'All versions of Natural Earth raster + vector map data found on this website are in the public domain.' No attribution required. NASA imagery page: 'The NASA Insignia, Logotype, identifiers, and imagery are not in the public domain.'; a paraphrase on the same page says NASA media generally falls outside US copyright. Design D's O-6 conflict stands; the basemap-only default is clean.
key_findings.evidence: WebFetch naturalearthdata.com terms; WebFetch nasa.gov brand-center images page, 2026-10-17.

key_findings.finding: GitHub terms and limits (live): 'You may only access and use GitHub Actions to develop and test your application(s).' The CDN prohibition begins 'don't use Actions as a content delivery network or as part of a serverless application' (excerpt cut off). Pages: 'Published GitHub Pages sites may be no larger than 1 GB.'; 'soft bandwidth limit of 100 GB per month'; the 10-builds-per-hour limit 'does not apply if you build and publish your site with a custom GitHub Actions workflow'; deployments 'will timeout if they take longer than 10 minutes'.

Prototype: the globe page used CesiumJS 1.146.0 from cdnjs on a flat path (prototype-globe.json); no three.js route is prototyped. It shows a canvas in headless Chromium (SwiftShader, not GPU), a text fallback when the library is blocked (cdn_blocked_run), 390 px with no horizontal scroll (bodyScrollWidth 390 = innerWidth 390), and a 127 s browser suite.

reasons: Fits the build as written: Python writes PNG overlays and SVG transects in the existing build (build.py:397-424 pattern). Leaflet 1.9.4 is vendored with a sha256 that matches the file (judge-rules); map.js already uses L.imageOverlay (map.js:287, design-c).
No library and no WebGL: works where WebGL2 is absent (K14). First visit about 0.95 MB and a 2-hour loop visit about 1.2 MB on the wire, with budgets (K6, K7).

Loop: a 7-frame one-hour window, or 12 frames for two hours (design-c P4). Needs new persistence code, because load_previous reads state.json only (build.py:472-478). Build-side reads 3.9 GB a month at 10 minutes (K8).

JS: six duties N1-N6, each with a reason. Replace N5 with Python-written as-of text plus the existing page-age check (base.html:47-62). Put the layer code in its own file rather than map.js (2,155 lines; ROADMAP Next 9 wants it smaller).
Failure surfacing: per-layer 'could not load' (N4); a failed product keeps its last verified frame with its age; gaps show as gaps. Each product step needs the never-raise contract (K11).
Tests and smoke: CONTRACTS and freshness keys in website/sources.py with a loud-failure test (sources.py:34 pattern); smoke_map extension on branch pushes only (website.yml:96-105).
Shares the cadence risk (K1): freshness states read stale most of the day until the schedule is fixed.
fatal_flaws: None for the echo raster. Decisions, not violations: cloud and Band 13 layers need DECISIONS entries for satellite kinds (D12 has none; DECISIONS.md:97-98) and counsel on the NOAA ACHA banner ('Access is restricted to approved users only', goes-aws.json).

scores.design: design-d (globe.html on the website; vendored three.js 0.186.1)
reasons: Native to the website: one build, globe.html generated like map.html (build.py:397-403), site-only data, vendored library with SPDX MIT headers, no second job, a documented loader within rule 4 (AGENTS.md:66-72).
First visit about 1.1 MB on the wire (K6), inside design D's own 3.0 MB gate. Its slow-link arithmetic is overstated; restate the gate in transfer bytes.
Largest fixed cost: three.js at 417 KB gzip and 2.12 MB raw, copied into every build (build.py:379). No minified build exists. Lock and test the sha256 of both files (design-b pattern).
Unprototyped: the only prototype is Cesium from cdnjs (K17). No real-phone WebGL2 check exists (K14).

Loop (phase 4): no persistence on the site (build.py:375-376; load_previous at 472-478). Build-side reads 39.7 GB a month at 10 minutes and about 10 MB per viewer visit (K7, K8). Only no loop, or an external store read by the build alone (R2 free tier, hosting-options r2-1 to r2-4), avoids both.

JS: 850 lines and 55 KB new (+39% lines, +48% bytes; K13). Page age, state words and focus would be copied unless factored out. Phase 3 adds hand-written GLSL, which rule 4 allows only as documented browser work.
Build coupling: a raising product skips the whole deploy (K11), and the cadence risk (K1) multiplies it.
Tests: the remote-URL scan is HTML-only (tests/test_site.py:464); smoke_globe.py runs only on branch pushes (website.yml:96-105); Playwright is unpinned (website.yml:99).
Vocabulary conflict with the live map (K12). Phones: WebGL2 on iOS 15 and later (K14); the text List covers the rest; no real-device check.
fatal_flaws: Phase 4 loop: no persistence path on the site (build.py:375-376). Decision O-10: no loop, live-site reads (about 40 GB a month at 10-minute cadence), or an external store read only by the build.
Earth texture (phase 1 option): licence conflict (K15). Decision O-6; the basemap-only default avoids it.
Satellite layers (phase 2): D12 has no satellite kind; a DECISIONS entry is needed first.
Radar staleness: 15 min (DECISIONS.md:97-98, 341) vs 30 min (gridded.py:53; sources.py:115). Decision O-9 before D's freshness table is written.
Actions terms (O-7) apply to the whole site build, not only the globe (K16).

reasons: Its server routes cannot run on a static host: /globe and /api/globe/* need Flask (design-a data_endpoints; app.py:204). The site has no server by decision (DECISIONS.md:315-316, 353-354). Its 15 JS duties and null-geometry and below-ground rules transfer; the routes would become static products.

CDN: Cesium 1.146.0 from cdnjs with sha384 integrity. AGENTS.md:71-72 forbids third-party code from a CDN. Vendoring Cesium.js costs about 1.8 MB on the wire (gzip-9 1,773,186 B, globe-libs.json), about 4x three.js, plus Workers (1,034,391 B) and Assets (4,379,545 B) raw, copied each build.

The bundled library contains a default ion access token string (judge-rules: five token-shaped strings). Shipping that code to the public site is a policy item. Ion-off overrides are not network-traced.

WebGL2 is required for voxels (1.134) and for labels (1.140+ unless the ANGLE extension is present), so the fallback is larger than design D's (globe-libs.json). VoxelPrimitive is experimental and @cesium/engine is removed in 1.150.
Strengths to keep: the 20-fixture alert parity test against alert_targets and the per-key freshness rule with a missing-key failure.
fatal_flaws: Server routes: the design as written cannot run on the site. The owner must accept a rewrite as static products. This is a design mismatch, not a rule breach; D27 keeps the desktop app parked (DECISIONS.md:314-323).

AGENTS rule 4 CDN clause (AGENTS.md:71-72): the default cannot be built under the written rule. Decision: amend rule 4 for the globe, or vendor Cesium (about 1.8 MB on the wire plus assets) under the Leaflet pattern.

scores.design: design-b (globe window in the desktop shell)
reasons: Built for the parked desktop app: a second private server in the shell, a read-only SQLite snapshot, per-OS installers and a decode child process (design-b components). The website has none of these and needs none (DECISIONS.md:314-323; AGENTS.md:7-14).
Installer churn, WebView2 and MSHTML WebGL2 limits and Windows decoding are desktop costs with no website benefit (design-b risks 2 and 4).

Transferable grafts: the sha384 lock file with a build-time check and a one-byte-change test; a schema number on each product that refuses unknown numbers; a 30-minute frozen-clock outage test; the 'not in JavaScript' list; the 14-day pin-age rule.
Its 13 duties (G-JS1 to G-JS13) are the clearest JS discipline of the four.
fatal_flaws: Reviving the desktop app: B cannot be built without an owner decision that names and reverses D27 (O1; DECISIONS.md:314-323). On the website the design's core is not needed; its grafts can be used without B.

AGENTS rule 2 (AGENTS.md:60-64): new pip packages need SHELL_API and min_shell raised, which design B's 'unchanged' claim does not reflect (round-1 finding stands). Owner ruling only if the desktop path is revived.

ranking_note: On this lens C2 is the lowest engineering risk and the lowest loop cost per visit. Design D is the only option that meets the globe request inside the website rules, so the globe question must be decided on the other lenses. This ranking does not make C2 a globe.
grafts_for_winner: From design D and gridded.py:991-1008: a never-raise contract with a status for every new product step, and a build test that one failing product leaves the other pages and state.json written. This protects the deploy (website.yml:162-163).

Freshness from timestamps, not notifications: write per-product last_run_utc, source_valid_utc and next_expected_utc into data/state.json (hosting-options ops graft). Show 'build late' text when now passes next_expected_utc; keep the 25-minute page check (base.html:58). Make the schedule fix (ROADMAP item 1) a precondition for any freshness claim.
Budgets in transfer bytes: a unit test that computes gzip sizes of every site file, and a branch-only transferSize check in smoke_map.py (K3).

New layer code in its own file (for example website/static/map/layers.js) with a line and byte cap test, so map.js does not grow. Move page-age and state-words code into one shared script rather than copying it (base.html:47-62; map.js page-age code).
Replace N5 with Python-written as-of text plus the existing page-age check (round-1 judge-rules graft; design-b G-JS4 pattern).
One words table in Python for hatch and no-data words (map.js:33-38; sources.py:116-117), decided once under the -99 and -999 decision (K12).

Test scope: scan every built HTML, JS and CSS file for remote http(s) URLs and CSS url(), not only index, about and map (tests/test_site.py:470-471). Keep the browser request-log check on branch pushes.
A sha256 lock file for vendored files with a build-time check and a one-byte-change test (design-b). Apply it to Leaflet now and to any later library.

If a loop is approved later: the build reads prior frames from an external store that only the build reads (R2 free tier: 10 GB storage and no egress charge, hosting-options r2-1 to r2-4). The browser stays site-only and the Pages soft limit is untouched. Needs O-10 and O-7.
Gate for any globe: add design D's three.js route only after C2's gates pass, with a prototype, a measured transfer budget (about 0.42 MB gzip) and a check on WebGL2-capable phones.
Invented sample layers carry DEMO labels and cannot reach the live publish (AGENTS rule 5; round-1 judge-rules graft).
Keep valid-time frame names (gridded.py:126-135). Measure ETag and transfer across two deploys in phase 1 before relying on browser reuse (K4).
corrections_to_designs: design-d.json s3 per_visitor_first_load and s2 slow_link_arithmetic: the three.js gzip estimate of about 0.62 MB is 1.46x high (measured 417,103 B GNU gzip -9; about 424,500 B on Pages). First visit is about 1.1 MB on the wire (computed), not 2.8 MB. D states 14 s at 1.6 Mbit/s; the wire figure is 5.5 s (computed; 17.7 s at 0.5 Mbit/s).
design-d.json s3 mrms: the 835,879 B peak is a 33-level, 20 dBZ keyframe (pipeline-options.json peak_keyframe), not the 11-level, three-threshold frame the design builds (K9).

design-d.json s3 pages_bandwidth and s7 phase 4: they count build-side reads (about 10 MB per build) but not viewer loop bytes (about 10 MB per visit). On wire bytes, 100 GB a month is about 90,000 first visits and about 9,000 loop visits, not 35,700 (computed).
design-d.json s6 test additions: the existing scan is HTML-only (tests/test_site.py:464); a JavaScript-level scan is needed.
design-d.json sources_used: the nasa.gov/multimedia/guidelines address returned HTTP 404 today; the sentence was found on the NASA brand-center images page (K15).
design-c.json P4: the 12-frame 0.9 MB loop is the right order of magnitude, and it is one reason C2 is cheaper per loop visit than D (K7).
judge-engineering.json (round 1): its 32-51 s build time was a sandbox figure; the runner median is 70 s (K2). Its Pages compression was unmeasured; it is now measured (K3).
main-architecture.json: 'cron every 10 min (website.yml:15)' is the configuration; measured scheduled starts are about every 146 minutes (median) (K1).
build.py:361-364: the comment says browsers and Pages reuse unchanged versioned files. Header evidence suggests a deploy may change the ETag (K4; unverified).
judge-rules.json: the base.html page-age script runs at lines 47-62, with the 25-minute test at line 58, not 49-57.
design-b.json: 'SHELL_API unchanged' conflicts with AGENTS.md:60-64 (round-1 finding stands).
owner_decisions: Schedule (ROADMAP item 1): explain or fix the 146-minute median gap between scheduled starts, and decide whether the 10-minute cron is a requirement. Decide who receives failure notices (GitHub sends scheduled-run notices to the schedule's creator, gh-notify-1). Until fixed, every freshness claim is conditional.
O-7 Actions terms: one reading for the whole site (develop and test vs publishing; the CDN prohibition, K16).
O-9 radar staleness: 15 or 30 minutes (DECISIONS.md:97-98 and 341 vs gridded.py:53; sources.py:115).
Words for MRMS -99 and -999: 'No radar coverage' or 'No radar data' (meanings unverified, mrms.json). One words table.
D12 satellite kinds and limits: a DECISIONS entry before any cloud or Band 13 layer; counsel on the ACHA banner (goes-aws.json).
O-6 Earth texture licence, only if design D's Earth layer is approved (K15). The basemap-only default avoids it.
O-10 loop: none, live-site reads (about 40 GB a month at 10-minute cadence; not recommended), or an external store read by the build alone.
Rule 4 for any library: a vendoring policy and a transfer-byte budget (three.js at 417 KB gzip), with a sha256 lock file.
O-5 phone floor: 288 px (smoke_pages.py:23) or 320 px (DESIGN.md:29-30).
